newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NEW FEDERAL MINIMUM AWARD WAGE OF $359.40
Workers earning less than 359-dollars-40 a week can now look forward to having their awards upgraded to that amount.
This follows the Industrial Relations Commission decision to establish a federal minimum award.
The Commission also approved a 10-dollar rise for workers on basic award levels, which should benefit about one-third of Australia's workers.
The decision comes following the ACTU's 20-dollar living wage claim, and its call for the setting of a minimum wage of 380-dollars.
The Commission said anything greater than a 10-dollar-a-week increase would jeapardise inflation targets and have adverse effects on employment.
LAWRENCE SAYS SHE'S INNOCENT AND WILL BE CLEARED
Federal Labor MP Carmen Lawrence, says she's bouyed by the public support she's received since last night's announcement she's facing perjury charges.
The former West Australian Premier is charged with three counts of perjury arising from evidence she gave to the Easton Royal Commission in 1995.
Dr Lawrence has stepped down from her position in the Shadow front bench, and says she's innocent and confident of beating the charges.
She says the charges result from her being forced to give her honestly held recollections to a politically motivated Royal Commission.
Her former senior advisor Ed Russell, and State M-P John Halden have also been charged over the matter, and Dr Lawrence and Mr Halden will appear in court on Thursday.
In WA, the charge of perjury carries a maximum penalty of 14 years jail.
$4.9 BILLION FOR VIC POWER STATION
Victoria's largest power station, Loy Yang A, has been sold for almost 4-point-9 Billion dollars, the world's highest price for an electricity trade sale.
It's also Australia's biggest-ever privatisation, and lifts proceeds from Victoria's electricity sell-off to more than 18 Billion dollars.
Loy Yang's buyer, Horizon Energy, is 75 percent U-S owned.
It says there are no plans to cut staff at the Latrobe Valley plant.
The Premier, Jeff Kennett, says the deal will cut two billion dollars from Victoria's debt, and put the state firmly on track to regain its Triple-A credit rating.
He predicts other states, particularly New South Wales, will now be forced to privatise electricity assets to compete with Victoria.
PRIVATISATION OF NSW TAB ANNOUNCED
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr says the State's TAB will be publicly floated providing it's at no loss to tax payers.
The Government formally announced its intention to privatise the TAB today, and State Cabinet has also endorsed plans to cut the wagering tax by almost half.
Bob Carr says the package will be put to the ALP Caucus soon.
He says the starting point for privatisation will be setting a price for the TAB which compensates the budget for the loss of the income flow.
He says the new TAB licence will prevent any shareholder from conducting other significant gaming or betting activities.
O'REILLY WANTS MEDIA FOREIGN OWNERSHIP LAWS RELAXED
Newspapaper and broadcasting executive Cameron O'Reilly says Australia's media cross-ownership laws should be retained but foreign ownership laws relaxed.
Mr O'Reilly, the chief executive of Australian Provincial Newspapers, says they would look at the John Fairfax group if those restrictions were lifted.
He was speaking at the annual meeting of Australian Provincial Newspapers, in which the Irish group Independent Newspapers has a 43 per cent stake.
Mr O'Reilly says the media requires foreign investment and foreign best practices, like any other industry.
HALE-BOPP IN WESTERN AUSTRALIAN SKIES
Western Australia will provide some of the best views of the Hale-Bopp comet over the next six weeks before the comet disappears for the next 3000 years.
Astronomer Peter Birch says as the comet gets higher in the sky over the next few weeks it will become visible to the naked eye.
He says at the moment it can be seen with binoculars and is quite bright and in a tear-drop shape.
Mr Birch says the best views will be north of Perth.
He says the comet's next appearance will be in July but its intensity will have faded considerably.
